paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the bias percentage in large language model (LLM) responses across three domains—Sports, Community, and Healthcare—before and after instruction tuning, categorized by the type of contact (no contact, positive contact, negative contact) used in the tuning process. The vertical axis represents "Bias Percentage" on a linear scale from 0 to 70, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists the three domains in left-to-right order: Sports, Community, and Healthcare. For each domain, there are three grouped bars, each corresponding to a contact type: "No Contact" (light gray), "Positive Contact" (light pink), and "Negative Contact" (light blue). Each of these is further subdivided into two stacked segments: the lighter shaded portion represents the bias percentage before instruction tuning, and the darker shaded portion (with diagonal hatching) represents the bias percentage after instruction tuning, starting from the top of the lighter bar. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color and pattern coding: light gray for "No Contact Before," light pink for "Positive Contact Before," light blue for "Negative Contact Before," gray with diagonal stripes for "No Contact After," red with diagonal stripes for "Positive Contact After," and blue with diagonal stripes for "Negative Contact After." In the Sports domain, the bias percentages before tuning are 45.42% (No Contact), 43.65% (Positive Contact), and 50.05% (Negative Contact), with corresponding reductions after tuning to 7.45%, 8.31%, and 8.33%, respectively. In the Community domain, bias before tuning is 38.08% (No Contact), 35.38% (Positive Contact), and 40.79% (Negative Contact), with negligible reductions after tuning (0.00%, 0.01%, and 0.00%, respectively). Similarly, in Healthcare, bias before tuning is 40.70% (No Contact), 37.51% (Positive Contact), and 46.73% (Negative Contact), with post-tuning values of 0.00%, 0.01%, and 0.11%, respectively. The dark bars are visually minimal in Community and Healthcare, indicating near-elimination of bias after instruction tuning, while in Sports, the dark bars remain relatively larger, suggesting less effective bias reduction. The bars are not sorted by height but are grouped by domain, and no specific bars are visually emphasized beyond the standard color and pattern coding.
